PAGE TITLE: MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS | WELCOME TO NASA
NASA Centers and Facilities

DIAGRAMS:
- Map of the United States showing locations of NASA centers, supporting facilities, and federally funded research and development centers.
- Legend:
  - Blue square: NASA center
  - Red circle: NASA supporting facility
  - Yellow hexagon: Federally funded research and development center
- Labeled locations on the map:
  - Ames Research Center (ARC)
  - Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL)
  - Armstrong Flight Research Center (AFRC)
  - White Sands Test Facility (managed by JSC)
  - Johnson Space Center (JSC)
  - Michoud Assembly Facility (managed by MSFC)
  - Stennis Space Center (SSC)
  - Neil A. Armstrong Test Facility (managed by GRC)
  - Glenn Research Center (GRC)
  - Katherine Johnson Verification and Validation Facility (managed by GSFC)
  - Goddard Institute for Space Studies (managed by GSFC)
  - Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC)
  - Wallops Flight Facility (managed by GSFC)
  - Mary W. Jackson Headquarters
  - Langley Research Center (LaRC)
  - Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC)
  - Kennedy Space Center (KSC)
  - NASA Shared Services Center (managed by SSC)

PHOTOS:
- Photo 1: Dragonfly team members review the half-scale lander model after it underwent wind tunnel testing at NASA Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia. Team members Art Azarbarzin, Juan Cruz, Wayne Dellinger, Zibi Turtle, Chuck Hebert, Ken Hibbard, Bernadine Juliano and Bruce Owens are utilizing unique NASA facilities to shape innovative Titan-bound Rotorcraft. Photo Credit — Johns Hopkins APL/Ed Whitman, October 23, 2023
- Photo 2: Technicians and engineers inside the Payload Hazardous Servicing Facility at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida inspect the Agency's largest planetary mission spacecraft, Europa Clipper, as part of prelaunch processing on Tuesday, May 28, 2024. Slated to launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket later this year from Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy, Europa Clipper will help determine if conditions exist below the surface Jupiter’s fourth largest moon, Europa that could support life. Photo Credit — NASA/Kim Shiflett
- Photo 3: Technicians at NASA’s Michoud Assembly Facility in New Orleans, lift a Liquid Oxygen Tank intended for Space Launch System (SLS) into Cell D. This tank will be crucial for the astronauts participating in the Artemis missions. NASA is working to land the first woman and first person of color on the Moon under Artemis. SLS is part of NASA’s backbone for deep space exploration, along with Orion and the Gateway in orbit around the Moon. SLS is the only rocket in operation that can send Orion, astronauts, and supplies to the Moon in a single mission. Photo Credit — NASA/Evan Deroche, February 01, 2024

KEY FACTS:
- Testing capabilities support future mission success for aircraft, spacecraft, and exploration vehicles.
